source_lines: ## 0. Sources and errors in the brief

**Trace.** The only full raw trace of the current Qwen plan is `results_tiles/tr_all.bin` [M]. It records 60,362 tasks on 304 workers, 8 XCDs x 38 (`results_tiles/tr_all.log:3`). The step is correct: 32/32 tokens equal to HF greedy (`results_tiles/tr_all.log:4`). The GPU was an AMD Instinct MI300X VF with 304 CUs and 8 XCCs (`results_tiles/pmc_all/pmc_agent_info.csv:3`). The ROCm version of that session is [U]. The build flags were `-DETX_DSL_WSUM -DETX_DSL_SCALAR -DETX_DSL_GU1 -DETX_DSL_RBATCH` (`results_tiles/build_all.log:2`). `ETX_VL_NT` was not set, so the non-temporal weight loads were on by default (`examples/vllm_llm/build.sh:55`).
**Plan.** `results_tiles` has no `plan.json`. This report uses `results_vlbest2_2026-10-10/b_all/plan.json`. That choice has three checks:
1. The plan text of both builds is identical. `results_tiles/vlplan_all.txt` and `results_vlbest2_2026-10-10/b_all/vl_plan.txt` have the same SHA256, `046be64d2fd14fe0...` [M].
2. Each of the 60,362 trace rows has the type, coordinates and worker that the plan assigns to that task. There are 0 mismatches [M].
3. Every task executed. Every grid is in static mode, and its domain is the physical XCD from `etx_amdgcn_xcc_id()` [M].

The critical path is a chain of 436 tasks. Its bodies and gaps sum exactly to the span: `3525.2 + 886.9 = 4412.1 us` (`report.txt:888`) [M]. All 435 gaps are dependency gaps. The queue gap is 0.0 us. The table cuts the same chain into the four classes of the brief (`account.txt:40-80`).
| Class | Part | us | % of span | Label and arithmetic |
| (a) bytes | phase bytes at 4.3 TB/s | 1439.6 | 32.6 | [E] 6.1904 GB / 4.3 TB/s. Each phase has one task on the path, so the path carries each phase's full floor once. |

| (a) bytes | exposed load round trips | 534.4 | 12.1 | [E] ISA hops x 0.50 us coherent or 0.104 us cached (`docs/FLOORS-2026-10-08.md:76-88,127-140`). The hop counts are from the round11 ISA, not this build. |
| (b) dependency | handoff after the producer, consumer's worker free | 653.1 | 14.8 | [M] `886.9 - 233.8` |
| (c) machinery | body above (a) | 1551.3 | 35.2 | [E] measured body minus the (a) estimate. 643.3 us is in the streaming phases and 908.0 us in the latency phases (`account.txt:56`). |
| (c) machinery | consumer's worker still in its previous task's arrive and queue fetch | 233.8 | 5.3 | [M] 138 of 435 edges (`account.txt:80`) |

source_lines: ### The implementable protocol: one prep owner, early publication, last partition reduces

Keep the current head-affine parallel partitions. Assign an owner for each `(step, layer, kv_head)`, with exactly one prep execution. The owner performs the existing q/k norm and RoPE, preserves its bf16 rounding and writes the current KV row once. After **all owner waves' stores have drained**, publish a head-local, epoch-qualified `prep_ready`. Publish it **before** the owner executes its attention partition, not at the end of the whole task. The other partitions acquire that publication and run their unchanged imported attention calls in parallel. The owner also runs its own partition.

Each partition writes the original bf16/fp32 partial buffers, drains all producing waves and arrives at a per-head completion counter. The last arrival executes the original imported reduce for that head. Election changes the worker, not the reduce's partition order. It must acquire visibility for **all** producers' partials before reduction; last arrival alone does not make those data loads safe. Publish the normal reduced-output event only after all reduce waves finish. The existing o_proj consumers then proceed.

This directly joins prep to the attention call and attention to reduce in the task body; it requires a new adapter/runtime protocol for **mid-body signals**, not a generic `pure` prologue fold. Import-round barriers must finish uniformly before reuse of a slot or before reduction. Static queues must place every producer before any blocked successor; a resident producer cannot be queued behind a waiting consumer on the same worker. A waiter must never monopolise the only execution resources its producer needs. Use discovered XCD identity, not block-index assumptions (`etx/machine/arch/gfx942.yaml:62,94,100`).

Norms surrounding this segment are part of the same audit: the input/residual norm is already folded into qkv, and the post-attention residual norm into router (`model.py:299-305`; `etx/ops/gemv.py:81-85`). Keep those folds and rounding points; do not book their removed launches again. The remaining imported input/final RMSNorm can be chained only with a consumer that fits the same ownership and visibility contract. A qkv or o_proj grid distributed across XCDs still needs its true fan-in/fan-out dependency. The isolated residual norm opportunity has **[U] zero separate credit**; it is not another attention boundary.

cannot be placed off the critical path at these boundaries: the consumer grids are as wide as the producer
grids (256 tasks = 32 per XCD against 38 workers; moe_up 192 = 24 per XCD), the next phase gates on **every**
consumer (event counts [256] and [24] in section 2), and only 6 of 38 workers per XCD are free after a
32-task phase (14 after moe_up's 24) [E arithmetic from the grid sizes, `tr_off.log:30-38`, and
`off_compile.log:2-3`]. So at least 18-26 consumers per XCD must start behind a producer on the same
worker, and the path, needing the last consumer, always pays one busy worker's arrive+fetch. 13 of the 48
moe_up -> moe_down critical consumers even sit on the critical producer's own worker (`account.txt:62`).
The measured attempt to move the fetch earlier, BAR2, made the step **+0.095 ms** slower
(`docs/BUDGET-2026-10-01.md:257`; mechanism `kernel.py:315-331`): the cost reappeared, larger.

source_lines: # BAR2: read the next head HERE, before the body, and keep it in registers. Issuing these two global loads
# after the drain (where they first sat) put an HBM round trip on the publication path -- every dependent
# worker waited for it, which measured +0.117 ms on 2026-10-01. Behind the body they cost nothing.
out.append("  if (threadIdx.x == 0 && cursor < cend) { nx_tid = p.static_queue[cursor]; nx_task = p.static_descs[cursor]; ++cursor; }")
out.append(f"  for (int j = 0; j < {max_pro}; ++j) if (psym[j] >= 0) {{ etx_call_body(psym[j], &pctx[j]); __syncthreads(); }}")
out.append("  etx_call_body(sym, &ctx);   // phase 2: the only call site of each body")
out.append("  ETX_RELEASE_DOMAIN();   // every wave drains its own stores before the barrier: thread 0's release only covers wave 0")
out.append("  // BAR2: publish the head fetched before the body into the other parity slot (write-after-read safe:")
out.append("  // the running task reads slot par, this writes par ^ 1); the barrier below broadcasts it for free.")
out.append("  // Registers only -- no global load between the drain and the barrier, which is the publication path.")

the poll granularity and the touch barrier is **[U]** — the trace cannot separate them (section 5).

The probe divides the bytes of one task by the hw_stream rate of one workgroup. The rate at 256 workgroups is an interpolation. Source: `docs/BUDGET-2026-10-01.md:86-90`.
The `hw_cohload.log` median of one workgroup is 0.28 us. The 0.50 us value is the span over all workgroups.
Each hop class has one price:
1. A coherent load (`sc1`) and the drain of a coherent store cost one coherent round trip.
2. A plain load costs the cached price. After an acquire (`buffer_inv sc1`), a plain load misses L2 and costs one coherent round trip. attn, reduce, in_norm and argmax start after an acquire.
3. A scalar load, a scratch reload and the drain of a plain store cost the cached price.
4. An LDS step costs nothing in the floor. The tables report it separately.

sentence: (`docs/BUDGET-2026-10-01.md:161`) and fabric one-ways of 642/742 ns (`gfx942.yaml:69-70`). Nine
context:
1. **The chain pays the boundary count, not an above-floor price.** Every free-consumer edge measures
   1.08-1.20 us same-XCD and 1.40-1.96 cross-XCD (section 2), against the measured 1.00 us/edge floor
   (`docs/BUDGET-2026-10-01.md:161`) and fabric one-ways of 642/742 ns (`gfx942.yaml:69-70`). Nine
   boundaries per layer times 48 layers at that floor is most of the 871.0 us no matter what protocol moves
   the bits. Fewer boundaries means fusing bodies, and fusion deletes only the flag round trip: the drain
   and the publication survive inside the fused body for every non-owner consumer
   (`docs/PLAN-300TOKS-2026-10-11.md:66-68`).
2. **The busy half is work conservation under full-barrier events.** Consumer grids are as wide as producer
   grids, every consumer gates the next phase (event counts [256], [24]), and only 6-14 of 38 workers per
   XCD are free at a boundary (section 3, (ii)). Some consumer on the path must start behind a producer on
   the same worker; 13 of 48 critical moe_up -> moe_down consumers sit on the critical producer's own
   worker (`account.txt:62`). The one measured attempt to move the fetch earlier cost +0.095 ms
   (`docs/BUDGET-2026-10-01.md:257`).
3. **The escapes are redesigns, not protocol changes.** Narrowing a consumer grid to the idle pool
   lengthens its bodies proportionally (fewer workers stream the same bytes per phase). Fusing the wide
   pairs moves the wait mid-body: the MoE fold is an XCD-local all-to-all of 24 producers (event E_8,
   counts [24]), so a fused moe_up+moe_down task still polls the same flag between its halves.

source_lines: Keep the current head-affine parallel partitions. Assign an owner for each `(step, layer, kv_head)`, with exactly one prep execution. The owner performs the existing q/k norm and RoPE, preserves its bf16 rounding and writes the current KV row once. After **all owner waves' stores have drained**, publish a head-local, epoch-qualified `prep_ready`. Publish it **before** the owner executes its attention partition, not at the end of the whole task. The other partitions acquire that publication and run their unchanged imported attention calls in parallel. The owner also runs its own partition.

Each partition writes the original bf16/fp32 partial buffers, drains all producing waves and arrives at a per-head completion counter. The last arrival executes the original imported reduce for that head. Election changes the worker, not the reduce's partition order. It must acquire visibility for **all** producers' partials before reduction; last arrival alone does not make those data loads safe. Publish the normal reduced-output event only after all reduce waves finish. The existing o_proj consumers then proceed.

source_lines: """Bandwidth-aware simulation of a compiled plan on the XCDs of one GPU.
Where etx.sim.protocol gives every task a fixed duration, this one gives it a cost *shape* and lets the tasks that run at
the same time share the memory system, so what one XCD does changes what another gets:
task = wait (its input events, each fired at its last producer's end + the release, seen after the hand-off of the
event's scope) -> front + floor + etx (fixed: the hardware minimum a workgroup pays before its bytes, plus
ETX's own acquire / argument / release cost) -> chain (fixed: the kernel's dependent global round trips,
barriers, reductions) -> stream (bytes, fluid: rate-limited per CU and sharing the GPU's bandwidth) -> end
Since 2026-09-30 the fixed part is dominated by `floor_us` and `etx_us`, measured per phase rather than derived from
an instruction count: hw_bench stream shows 296 workgroups cost about 3 us even when they read 896 B each, and the
measured builds put ETX's own share on top of that (docs/MODEL-vllm-kernels.md section 19). The earlier model
charged a per-task tax of about 2 us and counted events, and predicted gains from folding that the hardware did not
pay: build 2 5.934 ms -> build 3 5.895 ms, against a predicted 0.9 ms.
Streams follow Little's law: all of them see one loaded latency L = max(idle round trip, bytes in flight on the GPU /
bandwidth), and each pulls its bytes in flight / (L + the work of a trip that is not overlapped with memory). So a GPU

full of streams is bandwidth-bound, a few streams are latency-bound, and an XCD that streams alone runs faster. Workers run their static queue in order, one task at a time (the generated kernel's loop).

sentence: 2. **The router's real rows are all on XCD 0-3.** The router has M = 128 rows on a grid of 256 tasks. That gives `ceil(128 / 256) = 1` row per task (`examples/vllm_llm/model.py:289-291,343`). Tasks 0-127 have the rows and are on XCD 0-3. Tasks 128-255 are on XCD 4-7 and have no row. Their bodies take 0.28 us, against 5.20 us on XCD 0-3 (median over all layers) [M]. The router finish skew between XCDs is about 6 us in every layer (`docs/xcd-timeline-2026-10-11/report.txt:459,468,477`).
context:
Three facts explain the per-XCD shape:
1. **prep, attn and reduce run only on XCD 0-3.** Their grids have 4, 20 and 4 tasks (`results_vlbest2_2026-10-10/b_all/plan.json`, `types` and `descs`) [M]. For about 21 us of each 89 us layer, XCD 4-7 run no task body at all. The sum is `1.31 + 4.19 + 0.64 + 6.24 + 0.36 + 6.48 + 1.72 = 20.94 us` [E].
2. **The router's real rows are all on XCD 0-3.** The router has M = 128 rows on a grid of 256 tasks. That gives `ceil(128 / 256) = 1` row per task (`examples/vllm_llm/model.py:289-291,343`). Tasks 0-127 have the rows and are on XCD 0-3. Tasks 128-255 are on XCD 4-7 and have no row. Their bodies take 0.28 us, against 5.20 us on XCD 0-3 (median over all layers) [M]. The router finish skew between XCDs is about 6 us in every layer (`docs/xcd-timeline-2026-10-11/report.txt:459,468,477`).
3. **The streaming phases use 24 or 32 of the 38 workers of each XCD.** qkv, o_proj, router and moe_down have 256 tasks, moe_up has 192 (`docs/xcd-timeline-2026-10-11/latency.txt:5-13`). No worker gets two tasks of one grid in the whole step [M].

For about 21 us of each 89 us layer, XCD 4-7 run no task body at all. The sum is `1.31 + 4.19 + 0.64 + 6.24 + 0.36 + 6.48 + 1.72 = 20.94 us` [E].
2. **The router's real rows are all on XCD 0-3.** The router has M = 128 rows on a grid of 256 tasks. That gives `ceil(128 / 256) = 1` row per task (`examples/vllm_llm/model.py:289-291,343`). Tasks 0-127 have the rows and are on XCD 0-3. Tasks 128-255 are on XCD 4-7 and have no row. Their bodies take 0.28 us, against 5.20 us on XCD 0-3 (median over all layers) [M]. The router finish skew between XCDs is about 6 us in every layer (`docs/xcd-timeline-2026-10-11/report.txt:459,468,477`).
3. **The streaming phases use 24 or 32 of the 38 workers of each XCD.** qkv, o_proj, router and moe_down have 256 tasks, moe_up has 192 (`docs/xcd-timeline-2026-10-11/latency.txt:5-13`). No worker gets two tasks of one grid in the whole step [M].

Class definitions, all per worker:
- **dep**: the worker took the task, and the last producer's body still runs.
- **handoff**: from the last producer's body done, or from the take if that is later, to deps ready. This is the producer's arrive, event visibility, the poll, the touch, the acquire, the context setup and one barrier.
- **between**: from the previous task's body done to the take of the next task. This is the untimed arrive of the previous task and the static-queue fetch. The mean is `81840.9 / 60058 = 1.36 us` per task [E] (`account.txt:5`).
- **bytes**: the phase's bytes at 4.3 TB/s plus the exposed load round trips from the ISA hop table, capped at the body (`docs/FLOORS-2026-10-08.md:84-88,127-140`). This is an estimate, because nothing inside a body is stamped.
- **machinery**: the rest of the body.
- **none**: after the worker's last task.

source_lines: Each hop class has one price:
1. A coherent load (`sc1`) and the drain of a coherent store cost one coherent round trip.
2. A plain load costs the cached price. After an acquire (`buffer_inv sc1`), a plain load misses L2 and costs one coherent round trip. attn, reduce, in_norm and argmax start after an acquire.
3. A scalar load, a scratch reload and the drain of a plain store cost the cached price.
4. An LDS step costs nothing in the floor. The tables report it separately.

sentence: 1. **KV in the Infinity Cache.** The attention bytes at 4.3 TB/s take 24.1 us on the critical path (`account.txt:48`). At the Infinity Cache rate of 11.9 TB/s (`docs/SURVEY-2026-09-29.md:17`) they take `24.1 x 4.3 / 11.9 = 8.7 us`. The largest saving is `24.1 - 8.7 = 15.4 us`, 0.35% of the span. The streaming benchmark shows a smaller effect at 104 MB: 3.43 TB/s cold, 3.66 warm and 3.74 from the Infinity Cache (`results_2026-09-27/vlnext/overlap.log:6`). attn is latency-bound: its phase reaches 7.8% of the bandwidth (`bandwidth.txt:9`) **[17.1% of its own 3.67-XCD ceiling, section 8.1; the latency-bound conclusion is unchanged]**.

**Upper bounds for the remaining cache levers [E].**
1. **KV in the Infinity Cache.** The attention bytes at 4.3 TB/s take 24.1 us on the critical path (`account.txt:48`). At the Infinity Cache rate of 11.9 TB/s (`docs/SURVEY-2026-09-29.md:17`) they take `24.1 x 4.3 / 11.9 = 8.7 us`. The largest saving is `24.1 - 8.7 = 15.4 us`, 0.35% of the span. The streaming benchmark shows a smaller effect at 104 MB: 3.43 TB/s cold, 3.66 warm and 3.74 from the Infinity Cache (`results_2026-09-27/vlnext/overlap.log:6`). attn is latency-bound: its phase reaches 7.8% of the bandwidth (`bandwidth.txt:9`) **[17.1% of its own 3.67-XCD ceiling, section 8.1; the latency-bound conclusion is unchanged]**.
2. **The latency phases' loads.** Their activation loads are coherent, so they go past the XCD's L2 by design (`etx/codegen/kernel.py:296-299`). Cross-XCD data must take that path, so a higher L2 hit rate cannot shorten these hops. The round trip under load is 0.69 to 0.73 us at every level, L2, MALL or HBM (`docs/MODEL-vllm-kernels.md:321`). Queueing sets it, not the cache level.
3. **Cacheable weights.** fleet made the router and kv_b weights cacheable on the same GPU. The result was 18% slower, because the working set passed the 4 MB per-XCD L2 cliff (`~/code/fleet-mi300x/docs/STATUS.md:81,233`). fleet's idle-worker prefetch into the Infinity Cache gave no gain (`STATUS.md:72`).

1. **KV in the Infinity Cache.** The attention bytes at 4.3 TB/s take 24.1 us on the critical path (`account.txt:48`). 2. **The latency phases' loads.** Their activation loads are coherent, so they go past the XCD's L2 by design (`etx/codegen/kernel.py:296-299`). Cross-XCD data must take that path, so a higher L2 hit rate cannot shorten these hops. The round trip under load is 0.69 to 0.73 us at every level, L2, MALL or HBM (`docs/MODEL-vllm-kernels.md:321`). Queueing sets it, not the cache level.
3. **Cacheable weights.** fleet made the router and kv_b weights cacheable on the same GPU. The result was 18% slower, because the working set passed the 4 MB per-XCD L2 cliff (`~/code/fleet-mi300x/docs/STATUS.md:81,233`). fleet's idle-worker prefetch into the Infinity Cache gave no gain (`STATUS.md:72`).

Thresholds, registered before the run:
- The cache is a factor only if the NT pair moves the wall by at least 0.030 ms, the repository's KEEP cut (`docs/PLAN-300TOKS-2026-10-11.md:157`), or if L2 misses per step exceed `6.1904 GB / 119.5 B = 51.8 M` [E] by more than 10%. A miss count above that means read amplification.
- If neither holds, close the cache question for this plan and do not fund cache work.

sentence: 1. **Bodies of the latency phases: 1304.4 us, 29.6% [E].** topk, router, prep, attn, reduce, argmax, in_norm and the prologue have critical bodies of 371.6, 240.6, 184.7, 264.3, 258.4, 9.4, 3.8 and 2.2 us (`latency.txt:3-15`). Together they move 0.13 GB, 2.1% of the bytes (`bandwidth.txt:3-15`). The term is their exposed hops, 396.4 us [E], plus their residual machinery, 908.0 us [E] (`account.txt:42-57`). During these phases the machine draws less than 25% of the bandwidth. The low-bandwidth time by phase is topk 401.5, router 328.0, attn 310.0, reduce 308.5 and prep 225.0 us (`report.txt:1328-1338`). The router's 128 tasks with rows and the 4-, 20- and 4-task attention grids keep 300 workers idle, as section 1 shows.

2. **Dependency gaps: 886.9 us, 20.1% [M].** The path has 435 handoffs, a mean of `886.9 / 435 = 2.04 us` [E]. The busy-consumer edges after the wide phases cost the most (section 2.2). In 138 edges the consumer's worker was still busy with its previous task. That part alone is 233.8 us [M].
3. **Streaming phases below full rate: 781.3 us, 17.7% [E].** moe_up, moe_down, qkv, o_proj and lm_head have critical bodies of 835.8, 474.6, 445.2, 277.0 and 157.4 us (`latency.txt:5-14`). The excess is 138.0 us of hops before the first weight load and 643.3 us of residual [E]. The residual holds the norm fold, the x staging into LDS, the reductions and the store drains. Per-task start costs matter because each task streams only 0.07 to 0.26 MB [E]: 16.777 MB / 256 for o_proj, 50.332 MB / 192 for moe_up.

context:
1. **Intra-body stamps.** The bytes and machinery split of every body is an estimate (section 2.1). An optional second trace level could stamp, in the DSL tiles, the first weight load issued, the last weight load returned and the start of the store drain. The imported attention and reduce bodies cannot carry stamps without a change to the imported code [U].
2. **An arrive stamp.** The arrive after `tr[2]` is not stamped (`etx/codegen/kernel.py:333-335`). It is inside the 233.8 us of late edges and inside every gap. One more int64 per trace row would measure it. The row is now 9 int64 (`etx/tools/timeline.py:71-78`, 72 B per task).
3. **A poll-success stamp in phase 1.** It would split each gap into visibility and the rest: touch, acquire, context setup and the barrier. It would show whether the touch is exposed in the busy-consumer edges. A cheaper first test exists: an A/B of the `-DETX_NO_TOUCH` build (`etx/codegen/kernel.py:287`). `docs/OPTIMISATIONS.md:27` says the touch was never isolated after `ETX_VL_COH`.
4. **Per-phase counters.** rocprofv3 reports one value per dispatch, and one dispatch is a whole step. No tool gives L2 hits per phase. rocprofv3 thread trace could time each wave's instructions. Its support on this VF is [U].
5. **An Infinity Cache counter.** None of the data sets has one. Section 3 step 1 checks whether the VF exposes one.
6. **Fixed in this report:** `etx.tools.timeline` grouped the low-bandwidth time by phase kind with a regex that kept the `_x` suffix of replicated grids. Each `topk_N_x` was a separate kind, so topk dropped out of the list. topk is in fact the largest low-bandwidth kind at 401.5 us. The fix is at `etx/tools/timeline.py:296`. The same suffix also gave each topk layer its own colour in the HTML page (`timeline.py:497-499`). A test covers the grouping (`tests/test_timeline.py`).
7. **Session fetch.** `tools/session.sh:89` excludes `b_*/`, so a fetched session has no `plan.json` and no `vl_plan.txt`. This report had to borrow the plan of another session and check it row by row. A copy of both files to the session root, as `qwen300.py` already does for `compile.log`, `hipcc.log` and `compiler_version.txt`, would remove that step.
8. **Trace every timed build.** The anchor session timed a build that it never traced. A session that traces the build it times removes the build caveat of section 0. qwen300 does this (section 6).

sentence: The per-phase bandwidth shares above divide each phase's achieved GB/s by the whole device's 4.3 TB/s. No phase runs on all eight XCDs. `latency.txt` already measures the per-phase `XCDs live` column (`docs/xcd-timeline-2026-10-11/latency.txt:5-14`). One XCD's share of the achievable 4.3 TB/s is `4.3 / 8 = 0.5375 TB/s` [E], so a phase's own ceiling is `XCDs live x 0.5375 TB/s`, and its share of that ceiling is the only bandwidth number that means anything for it. A phase on four XCDs could never have reached 4.3 TB/s; comparing it to 4.3 TB/s makes latency-bound phases look like they waste bandwidth they never had.

source_lines: The anchor is Qwen3-30B-A3B, bf16, batch one, context 1024, one MI300X **VF**, ROCm 7.14.0, five rounds of **host wall** measurements (`results_vlbest2_2026-10-10/report.log:3-11`). The fused wall median is **4.471 ms [M]**, the same-kernel HIP graph **4.654 ms [M]**, default vLLM **4.855 ms [M]**, and strongest tested legal vLLM, S3/unified AITER attention, **4.749 ms [M]** (same source). Thus `1000 / 4.471 = 223.7 tok/s`, target `1000 / 300 = 3.333333 ms`, required cut `4.471 - 3.333333 = 1.137667 ≈ 1.138 ms`, or `1.137667 / 4.471 = 25.45% [E]`.

sentence: One precision about what "idle" means here. `any body` marks an XCD busy when at least one of its 38 workers is in a task body. At worker granularity the busy share is lower: bodies cover 40.03% of worker-time (bytes 27.57% + machinery 12.46%, `account.txt:8-9`), and 53.00% of worker-time is dependency wait (`account.txt:6-7`). A worker in a dependency wait has already taken its next task and still occupies its CU; the 27.06% counts XCDs with no body at all, where all 38 workers are waiting or done. Both numbers matter below: the first says how much work could in principle be re-issued, the second says how much of the machine has nothing issued at all.

source_lines: The anchor is Qwen3-30B-A3B, bf16, batch one, context 1024, one MI300X **VF**, ROCm 7.14.0, five rounds of **host wall** measurements (`results_vlbest2_2026-10-10/report.log:3-11`). The fused wall median is **4.471 ms [M]**, the same-kernel HIP graph **4.654 ms [M]**, default vLLM **4.855 ms [M]**, and strongest tested legal vLLM, S3/unified AITER attention, **4.749 ms [M]** (same source). Thus `1000 / 4.471 = 223.7 tok/s`, target `1000 / 300 = 3.333333 ms`, required cut `4.471 - 3.333333 = 1.137667 ≈ 1.138 ms`, or `1.137667 / 4.471 = 25.45% [E]`.

sentence: **L2 (4 MB per XCD, private).** A prefetch lands in the L2 of the XCD that issues it, so an L2 window only works when prefetcher and consumer are the same XCD. What fits per XCD: qkv, o_proj, moe_down and everything smaller; moe_up (6.29 MB) and a whole layer (14.5 MB) do not. Fleet hit this cliff on the same GPU: making 113 MB of weights cacheable pushed the working set past the 4 MB per-XCD L2 and ran 18% slower (fleet `docs/STATUS.md:81,233`).

sentence: **The window is one layer, and what governs it is the 256 MB MALL minus the 104 MB resident KV cache.** In L2 the window is at most one moe_down-sized phase per XCD, governed by the 4 MB cliff. One phase-specific limit governs separately: moe_up's *selected* weights are 50.33 MB, but which experts are selected is only known when topk finishes, 1.08 us (median) before moe_up starts (`account.txt:72`). Prefetching all 128 experts instead of the 8 selected is `50.33 x 128 / 8 = 805.3 MB` per layer [E] (`examples/llm/configs/qwen3-30b-a3b.json:1`: 128 experts, 8 per token), 5.3 times the MALL headroom. moe_up is therefore not prefetchable in practice; its window collapses to the 1.08 us topk-to-moe_up gap.

context:
- The rate difference is measured, and it is small. `bench/overlap/overlap_bench.hip`'s stream mode on this GPU (`results_2026-09-27/vlnext/overlap.log:2-8`) [M]: at 104 MB, cold 3.43 TB/s, warm 3.66, from the Infinity Cache 3.74 (+9.0%); at 192 MB, cold 3.61, IC 4.23 (+17.2%); at 17.3, 34.6 and 64 MB the cache-resident pass is **slower** than cold (2.32/1.72, 3.03/2.45, 3.30/3.20). Residency helps only at layer-size windows, and there by about 9%.
- Load *latency* does not depend on the level under load: the round trip is 0.73 / 0.71 / 0.69 us at L2 / MALL / HBM with 303 CUs streaming (`docs/MODEL-vllm-kernels.md:321`) [M]. Queueing sets it, not the cache level. So caching cannot shorten the 534.4 us of exposed load round trips on the critical path (`account.txt:55`), including the 138.0 us of hops before the first weight load in the streaming phases.
- Today's consumer weight loads are non-temporal by default (`examples/vllm_llm/build.sh:52-55`, `etx/ops/gemv.py:124-126`): they are chosen so the 6.08 GB weight stream does not evict the MALL-resident KV cache. Whether an NT consumer load can even *hit* a prefetched MALL line is [U]. If it cannot, the consumer phases must switch to cached loads, which is exactly the change fleet measured at 18% slower when applied broadly (fleet `docs/STATUS.md:81`).
- What the repo does not know [U]: the MALL's eviction policy and any MALL hit counter. The timeline report's section 3 records that no data set has a MALL counter and that TCC counters cannot distinguish an Infinity Cache hit from an HBM read; the L2 is 4 MB per XCD. Eviction survival is therefore decidable today only by timing and by DRAM re-read counts, not by a hit counter.

- The rate difference is measured, and it is small. `bench/overlap/overlap_bench.hip`'s stream mode on this GPU (`results_2026-09-27/vlnext/overlap.log:2-8`) [M]: at 104 MB, cold 3.43 TB/s, warm 3.66, from the Infinity Cache 3.74 (+9.0%); at 192 MB, cold 3.61, IC 4.23 (+17.2%); at 17.3, 34.6 and 64 MB the cache-resident pass is **slower** than cold (2.32/1.72, 3.03/2.45, 3.30/3.20). Residency helps only at layer-size windows, and there by about 9%.
- Load *latency* does not depend on the level under load: the round trip is 0.73 / 0.71 / 0.69 us at L2 / MALL / HBM with 303 CUs streaming (`docs/MODEL-vllm-kernels.md:321`) [M]. Queueing sets it, not the cache level. So caching cannot shorten the 534.4 us of exposed load round trips on the critical path (`account.txt:55`), including the 138.0 us of hops before the first weight load in the streaming phases.

Whether an NT consumer load can even *hit* a prefetched MALL line is [U]. If it cannot, the consumer phases must switch to cached loads, which is exactly the change fleet measured at 18% slower when applied broadly (fleet `docs/STATUS.md:81`).
- What the repo does not know [U]: the MALL's eviction policy and any MALL hit counter. The timeline report's section 3 records that no data set has a MALL counter and that TCC counters cannot distinguish an Infinity Cache hit from an HBM read; the L2 is 4 MB per XCD. Eviction survival is therefore decidable today only by timing and by DRAM re-read counts, not by a hit counter.

sentence: **The eviction risk, stated plainly:** if a prefetched line is evicted before the consumer reads it, the line is read from DRAM twice — once by the prefetcher, once by the consumer — and the step is slower, not faster, by the prefetch's own traffic. The experiment detects this two ways: (a) `rocprofv3`'s `TCC_EA0_RDREQ_DRAM_sum` per dispatch, compared against the control arm; the baseline is 48.9-50.9 M requests at 119.5 B per request, one fetch per weight byte (`results_2026-10-01/round15/cache.txt:3-5`, `ntc.txt:1-3`, `results_2026-10-01/round15/FINDING.md:55-56`) [M], so any excess over the known 6.19 GB is re-reads; (b) the pass-C rate in the survival arm of the microbenchmark (section 5), which falls back to the cold rate if the window was evicted.

sentence: **Compute: no pair of phases is independent.** The decoder layer is a serial chain, qkv -> prep -> attn -> reduce -> o_proj -> router -> topk -> moe_up -> moe_down -> next layer's qkv (the layer order of `account.txt:82-143`), and every consecutive pair carries a measured dependency edge in the trace (`account.txt:62-79`). The brief's example needs a correction here: layer N's `attn` and `reduce` are indeed dependent, but layer N's `moe_down` and layer N+1's `qkv` are **not** independent either — the trace measures 47 such edges and 190.2 us of gaps on them (`account.txt:63,65`) [M], because qkv_{N+1} reads the residual stream that moe_down_N produces (the input/residual norm is folded into qkv). What is independent of everything is the **weight stream**: weights are constants, so any phase's weights can be loaded during any earlier phase, subject to capacity (section 1) and to the addresses being known (moe_up/moe_down only after topk).

sentence: Why the realised value will be lower than even 63 us: (a) the +9% was measured with no co-running consumer stream; during P2/P3 the prefetch competes with the running phase for the same HBM, and the measured price of filling idle bandwidth next to a latency chain is a doubling of its round trip, 1.52 -> 3.08 us (`overlap.log:15-16`, split placement, background 4.31 TB/s) — the latency phases carry 396.4 us of exposed hops [E], so even a 10% slowdown there (~40 us) eats most of the central estimate; (b) the MALL window sits at 86% occupancy with the KV cache, so some eviction is likely and every evicted line is read twice (section 2); (c) if NT consumer loads cannot hit the prefetched lines [U], the consumers must go cacheable, risking the fleet 18% L2-cliff loss; (d) fleet already measured this mechanism's two direct ancestors on the same GPU: idle-worker prefetch into the Infinity Cache gave no gain, and prefetch across the event wait was 4% slower (fleet `docs/STATUS.md:72,30`).

sentence: 1. **The idle is a symptom, not a resource.** A worker idles because its next task's inputs do not exist yet. Section 3 shows there is no independent compute to give it: every consecutive phase pair is dependency-linked in the trace, including the pair the brief calls independent (moe_down_N -> qkv_{N+1}, 47 measured edges, `account.txt:63,65`). The only thing that can move into the idle time is weight traffic, and weight traffic's value is bounded by the cache-rate delta, measured at +9% at layer size and negative at window size (`overlap.log:3-8`).
context:
1. **The idle is a symptom, not a resource.** A worker idles because its next task's inputs do not exist yet. Section 3 shows there is no independent compute to give it: every consecutive phase pair is dependency-linked in the trace, including the pair the brief calls independent (moe_down_N -> qkv_{N+1}, 47 measured edges, `account.txt:63,65`). The only thing that can move into the idle time is weight traffic, and weight traffic's value is bounded by the cache-rate delta, measured at +9% at layer size and negative at window size (`overlap.log:3-8`).
2. **Filling the idle ports has a measured price on the work that matters.** The fold benchmark on this GPU: the latency chain's round trip went 1.52 -> 3.08 us when a background stream filled the idle bandwidth (`overlap.log:15-16`). The latency phases carry 396.4 us of exposed hops [E]; a slowdown there is paid on the critical path, while the prefetch benefit is bounded at 63-121 us [E]. The mechanism can be net negative even when it works.
3. **It has been tried, twice, on this GPU.** Fleet's idle-worker prefetch of routing-independent weights into the Infinity Cache: no gain, 4.84 vs 4.80 ms, with the reason recorded — the per-CU streaming rate (~30 GB/s) caps what idle workers can pull, and the phases that would benefit are latency-bound, not byte-bound (fleet `docs/STATUS.md:72`). Cross-task prefetch across the event wait: 4% slower (fleet `docs/STATUS.md:30`). And ETX's own touch hook is already the within-phase version of this mechanism — waves 1-15 pull the task's first weights into L2 during the dependency wait (`etx/codegen/kernel.py:283-290`) — and its value after `ETX_VL_COH` was never isolated (`docs/OPTIMISATIONS.md:27`).
4. **Caching cannot shorten the latency that dominates.** The loaded round trip is level-independent (`docs/MODEL-vllm-kernels.md:321`), so residency touches only bandwidth exposure, which section 4 bounds at 2.7% of the span in the most favourable case.

sentence: The evidence that settles it, in order: the existing `-DETX_NO_TOUCH` A/B (a 20-second existing-switch probe that prices the mechanism's already-shipped within-phase form, `docs/OPTIMISATIONS.md:27`); phase 1's S1/S2 (does a prefetched window survive the step's own NT traffic at all) and S3/S4/I1 (is there a benefit, and what does it cost the latency chain); then phase 2's KEEP vote. If S1 or S2 fails, the idle time is provably not usable by this mechanism at this model shape, and the counter-argument holds. If phase 1 passes and phase 2 still misses KEEP, the idle time is usable in principle but worth less than 0.030 ms — and the 300 tok/s question must be answered elsewhere.

sentence: The body is an **all-task mean for a layer**, not a measured particular task or the last task's critical body. Tasks run concurrently: do not multiply by the task count. Body timing includes `etx_call_body`, **all-wave store drain and its final barrier**, between `tr[1]` and `tr[2]` (`etx/codegen/kernel.py:314,323-333`). Event arrival, next-task fetch and dependency wait lie outside it. Source-tile end is thus not trace-body end.

source_lines: ## 0. Sources and errors in the brief

The critical path is a chain of 436 tasks. Its bodies and gaps sum exactly to the span: `3525.2 + 886.9 = 4412.1 us` (`report.txt:888`) [M]. All 435 gaps are dependency gaps. The queue gap is 0.0 us. The table cuts the same chain into the four classes of the brief (`account.txt:40-80`).
| Class | Part | us | % of span | Label and arithmetic |
| (a) bytes | phase bytes at 4.3 TB/s | 1439.6 | 32.6 | [E] 6.1904 GB / 4.3 TB/s. Each phase has one task on the path, so the path carries each phase's full floor once. |

| (a) bytes | exposed load round trips | 534.4 | 12.1 | [E] ISA hops x 0.50 us coherent or 0.104 us cached (`docs/FLOORS-2026-10-08.md:76-88,127-140`). The hop counts are from the round11 ISA, not this build. |
| (b) dependency | handoff after the producer, consumer's worker free | 653.1 | 14.8 | [M] `886.9 - 233.8` |
| (c) machinery | body above (a) | 1551.3 | 35.2 | [E] measured body minus the (a) estimate. 643.3 us is in the streaming phases and 908.0 us in the latency phases (`account.txt:56`). |
| (c) machinery | consumer's worker still in its previous task's arrive and queue fetch | 233.8 | 5.3 | [M] 138 of 435 edges (`account.txt:80`) |
| (d) launch | inside the span | 0 | 0 | [M] one launch per step, queue gap 0.0 |

**(d) outside the span.** Host work per step is the wall median minus the device median of the untraced runs. That is `4.548 - 4.405 = 0.143 ms` [E], or 3.1% of the 4.548 ms wall. In the anchor session it is `4.471 - 4.340 = 0.131 ms` (`results_vlbest2_2026-10-10/etx_r1.log:2118`).

sentence: The ladder is older again: **18.37/11.11 us [M]** controls versus **11.55/7.64 us [M]** NOVMEM (`etx/ops/gemv.py:17-29`; raw finding `results_2026-10-01/round37/FINDING.md:3-17`). NOVMEM **still loads one weight vector per wave**, reusing it; it is not literally zero weight reads (`gemv.py:237-245`). It retains dot, activation LDS reads and loop arithmetic, but changes dependencies and compiler scheduling and gives wrong output. Its marginal differences cannot be summed as exclusive phases.

source_lines: MoE residual, measured in-tile (2026-10-02, round 37; traced decode, layer-11 mean bodies, control run twice around
the ladder at 18.32/18.41 up and 10.82/11.39 down; every DSL_ABLATE_* build is timing-only WRONG output):
ONEPASS (gate, no up)       10.45          -     the second pass costs its own stream, consistent
NORED   (no wave_sum/epi)   15.45       8.64     reduction + coherent output stores 16% / 22%
NOLDS   (const x in dot)    17.81      10.68     the dot's LDS reads 3% -- the 8-float lane stride is NOT a conflict
NOVMEM  (one weight vector) 11.55       7.64     the critical path WITHOUT the stream is 63% of the body
Exposed VMEM (control - NOVMEM) is 6.8 us = 37% for up, 3.5 = 31% for down: the stream hides under the skeleton, so
the budget's "65-70% of achievable bandwidth" framing was wrong -- the tile is skeleton-bound, not stream-bound, and
no single rung owns >= 50%. ~6.5 us/task of the skeleton is loop/flush/drain machinery no rung isolates; separating
it needs in-kernel timestamps, not ablations. Closed as spread at the structural floor of this tile shape.

// K % 512 == 0: 16 B loads, 4 in flight per lane; K % 256 == 0: 8 B loads, 8 in flight: 64 KB per workgroup of 16 waves
// (the megakernel's 1024 threads; 16 per lane as examples/llm/gemv.h's 4-wave tiles spilled 359 VGPRs at 128 per lane)
// Half in-flight depth (8 dwords per lane) is the DEFAULT since round 34: 4.832 against 4.884 wall ms/token for
// the full depth (3 interleaved runs each, same box), VGPR/spill/occupancy identical (128/8/4) -- the win is VMEM
// queue pressure and 1 MB less code, not registers. Round 32's Little's-law headroom at full depth was 4.8x, so
// half still covers the latency 2.4x over. Occupancy itself CANNOT move here: the persistent kernel launches one
// 16-wave workgroup per CU, so 4 waves/SIMD is fixed by the grid, not by VGPRs -- forcing VGPR 64 via launch
// bounds left runtime occupancy at 4.000 and cost 2x in spill traffic (9.39 wall, 1678 spills). -DETX_DSL_U4
static __device__ __forceinline__ void dsl_gemv(const __hip_bfloat16* __restrict__ W, int K, const float* xs, int r0, int r1, float* part, Epi epi) {
#ifdef DSL_ABLATE_EPL4                                   // ablation: force the 8 B load path everywhere (moe_down's,
dsl_gemv_rows<4, DSL_UN>(W, K, xs, r0, r1, part, epi); // since K = 768 is not a multiple of 512) -- output stays correct
if (K % (ETX_WAVE_SIZE * 8) == 0) dsl_gemv_rows<8, DSL_UW>(W, K, xs, r0, r1, part, epi);
else if (K >= ETX_WAVE_SIZE * 8 && K % (ETX_WAVE_SIZE * 4) == 0) dsl_gemv_split(W, K, xs, r0, r1, part, epi);
else dsl_gemv_rows<4, DSL_UN>(W, K, xs, r0, r1, part, epi);

source_lines: """Up only: fixed K=2048, 32 gate and 32 up rows, 16 whole-row waves.
Each row preserves the wave sum and all virtual zero additions, including
the original partial's +0. The gate/up join is retained before SiLU. Down
uses the original emitter and receives no up ownership proof.
start = s.index('template <int EPL, int U, int NB, class Epi>')
end = s.index('template <int EPL, int U, class Epi>', start)
f = replace_one(f, '  const int per = (S + nw - 1) / nw, sb = wv * per, se = min(S, sb + per);',
'  const int per = 16, sb = wv * per, se = sb + per;')
f = replace_one(f, '  for (int i = (int)threadIdx.x; i < nw * nrt * NB; i += blockDim.x) pl[i] = 0.f;\n  __syncthreads();', '')
# WSUM and fallback are preprocessor alternatives: preserve each original wave sum.
f = f.replace('if (lane == 0) pl[(wv * nrt + cur) * NB + b] += v;',
'if (lane == 0) { float z = 0.f; for (int w2 = 0; w2 < 16; ++w2) z += w2 == wv ? (0.f + v) : 0.f; epi(r0 + cur, &z); }')
a = f.index('#ifdef DSL_ABLATE_NORED\n#pragma unroll\n  for (int b')
f = f[:a] + '  __syncthreads(); // all gate/up results visible before SiLU; no LDS reuse before this join\n' + f[b:]
f = f.replace('  typedef typename dsl_wvec<EPL>::T V;',
'  static_assert(EPL == 8 && NB == 1, "fixed up mapping only");\n  typedef typename dsl_wvec<EPL>::T V;')
old = 'if (d.K % (ETX_WAVE_SIZE * 8) == 0 && 2 * gn <= DSL_RCH && gp1 % gspr == 0 && gp2 % gspr == 0 && (gn * gspr) % gp2 == 0) {'
bf16_single_rows_nb<8, DSL_UW, 1>(We, d.K, 0, xs, r0, r0 + 2 * gn, part, [&](int r, const float* v) {
const int q = r - r0; g[q < gn ? q : d.rpt + q - gn] = dsl_bfr(v[0]); }, gn, (long long)(d.M - gn) * d.K);

source_lines: float* g = xs + d.K; float* part = g + 2 * d.rpt;
int* lids = (int*)(part + 16 * DSL_RCH); float* lwts = (float*)(lids + 16);   // top-k fold: R = k, mode 3 = renormalised
if (etx_wave() == 0 && etx_lane() == 0) { lids[s] = s; lwts[s] = 1.f; }       // ablation: slot s -> expert s (WRONG output)
if (d.mode >= 2) dsl_topk_lds(d.logits, d.E, d.R, d.mode == 3 ? 1 : 0, lids, lwts);
const int dsl_eid = d.mode >= 2 ? lids[s] : dsl_a_ldi(d.ids + (size_t)rq * d.srows + s);
const __hip_bfloat16* We = d.W + (size_t)dsl_eid * d.estride;     // g: 2 x rpt floats (rpt <= DSL_RCH, host-checked)

source_lines: static __device__ __forceinline__ void dsl_stage(const __hip_bfloat16* __restrict__ x, int K, float* xs) {   // bf16 -> fp32 LDS, 16 B per thread
__syncthreads(); return;          // ablation: the barrier without the fill (the dot then reads stale LDS: WRONG output)
for (int i = (int)threadIdx.x; i < K / 8; i += blockDim.x) {
// activation: two device-coherent 8 B loads (both stay in flight; the compiler places the waits)
const unsigned long long lo = dsl_a_ld64((const unsigned long long*)(x + 8 * i));
const unsigned long long hi = dsl_a_ld64((const unsigned long long*)(x + 8 * i) + 1);
dsl_u32x4 v; v[0] = (unsigned)(lo & 0xffffffffull); v[1] = (unsigned)(lo >> 32); v[2] = (unsigned)(hi & 0xffffffffull); v[3] = (unsigned)(hi >> 32);
const DSL_G dsl_u32x4* xv = (const DSL_G dsl_u32x4*)x;
for (int i = (int)threadIdx.x; i < K / 8; i += blockDim.x) {
for (int j = 0; j < 4; ++j) { xs[8 * i + 2 * j] = __uint_as_float(v[j] << 16); xs[8 * i + 2 * j + 1] = __uint_as_float(v[j] & 0xffff0000u); }

source_lines: out.append("  etx_call_body(sym, &ctx);   // phase 2: the only call site of each body")
out.append("  ETX_RELEASE_DOMAIN();   // every wave drains its own stores before the barrier: thread 0's release only covers wave 0")
out.append("  // BAR2: publish the head fetched before the body into the other parity slot (write-after-read safe:")
out.append("  // the running task reads slot par, this writes par ^ 1); the barrier below broadcasts it for free.")
out.append("  // Registers only -- no global load between the drain and the barrier, which is the publication path.")
out.append("  if (threadIdx.x == 0) { s_tid2[par ^ 1] = nx_tid; if (nx_tid >= 0) s_task2[par ^ 1] = nx_task; }")
out.append("  if (tr && threadIdx.x == 0) { tr[2] = (uint64_t)ETX_TIMER(); tr[3] = worker; }")

source_lines: `[M]` denotes an existing measurement under its cited conditions. `[E]` denotes arithmetic or a conditional estimate, with its calculation. `[U]` denotes an unmeasured mechanism; it contributes zero to the sum. Paths beginning `results_` refer to the local archive in `~/code/etx/`, not necessarily files tracked by this worktree. `fleet/` below means `~/code/fleet-mi300x/`. Short citations `model.py` and `build.sh` mean `examples/vllm_llm/`; `host.h` means `etx/runtime/include/etx/host.h`; `gemv.py` and `attnprep.py` mean `etx/ops/`. These sources were read locally, including fleet's status and raw occupancy result; no data was regenerated.

The anchor is Qwen3-30B-A3B, bf16, batch one, context 1024, one MI300X **VF**, ROCm 7.14.0, five rounds of **host wall** measurements (`results_vlbest2_2026-10-10/report.log:3-11`). The fused wall median is **4.471 ms [M]**, the same-kernel HIP graph **4.654 ms [M]**, default vLLM **4.855 ms [M]**, and strongest tested legal vLLM, S3/unified AITER attention, **4.749 ms [M]** (same source). Thus `1000 / 4.471 = 223.7 tok/s`, target `1000 / 300 = 3.333333 ms`, required cut `4.471 - 3.333333 = 1.137667 ≈ 1.138 ms`, or `1.137667 / 4.471 = 25.45% [E]`.

The device median is **4.340 ms [M]** in a timed round; `4.471 - 4.340 = 0.131 ms [E]` is a difference of medians, not an additive host profile (`results_vlbest2_2026-10-10/etx_r1.log:2117-2120`). In particular, the printed `tokens_per_s` there uses device time, whereas this target uses wall time (`examples/vllm_llm/host.hip:920-928`). Neither the already-established fusion gain nor the S0-to-S3 gain is an extra cut from today's fused anchor.

The latest reusable phase trace is the four-flag `all` build, correct **32/32 [M]**, device span **4.413 ms [M]** (`results_tiles/tr_all.log:2-5,443-445`). Its flags match the later timing build, but the session and compiler resources differ (`results_tiles/build_all.log:2-5`; `results_vlbest2_2026-10-10/build_chkx.log:2,17-33`). Phase allowances come from the current-trace rebasing in `docs/PLAN-generic-decoder-2026-10-08.md:222-231`. Transferring them to today's anchor is explicitly **[E]**. They are not a same-session decomposition of 4.471 ms. A new trace must rebase the sum before any GPU result is claimed.

source_lines: 3. `source.py:62` prepares an isolated **up-only** specialization for K=2048,
32 gate plus 32 up rows, rpt=32, sixteen waves and 1024 threads. Each wave
owns four complete rows. It removes empty partial zeroing and cross-wave
gathering; preserves the original wave sum and virtual zero additions in
original wave order, bf16 rounding and SiLU; and retains the gate/up join
before SiLU. The original path is the fallback. Down remains unchanged and
receives no up ownership proof. GPU byte equivalence is still required.

sentence: - **Wave sum:** WSUM lane 0 is the only defined result; retain its xor-tree order and lane mask (`gfx942.yaml:117-131`). Using another lane's partial or a sequential reduction changes dots.
context:
- **Wave sum:** WSUM lane 0 is the only defined result; retain its xor-tree order and lane mask (`gfx942.yaml:117-131`). Using another lane's partial or a sequential reduction changes dots.
- **bf16 rounding:** up must round gate and up **separately before SiLU×up**, then round output; down must multiply fp32 dot by ws **before** the final bf16 rounding (`G:13-15,159-160,777,790,832`). No conversion to reduced precision is proposed.
- **Partial order:** every original zero addition, including the deposit's initial +0, is part of the numerical reference. Dropping them without proof can change signed zero/exceptional behavior; test byte equivalence on captured finite model inputs and inspect compiler math flags. Preserve actual w2 order, never completion order.
- **LDS lifetime:** up gate and up rows are owned by different waves. Keep the join before SiLU; no successor may reuse xs/g until all consumers finish. The down epilogue changes thread ownership but not row ownership.
- **Payload visibility:** the original down output is emitted by wave 0's lanes; the rewrite emits from multiple waves. Every producing wave must drain before the existing publication barrier. A thread-0-only drain is unsafe (`kernel.py:324-332`). Coherent store flags must remain.
source_lines: // etx_wave_sum's butterfly (partners at lane distance 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1) with only lane 0's result defined, so each
// step need be exact only on the lanes lane 0 later reads: 32 by ds_bpermute, 16 by ds_swizzle's xor mode (exact in
// each 32-lane half), 8 by DPP row_ror:8 (= xor 8 inside a 16-lane row), 4 by row_shl:4 (lane i reads i + 4: exact
// on lanes 0-3, all the later steps read), 2 and 1 by quad_perm. Every lane lane 0 depends on adds the same two
// values as in etx_wave_sum, and fp32 addition commutes, so lane 0 is bit-identical; the other lanes hold partial
// sums. Replaces four of six LDS-pipe round trips and the per-step lane-index arithmetic of __shfl_xor.

source_lines: static __device__ __forceinline__ float dsl_silu(float g) { return g / (1.f + __expf(-g)); }
// rows [r0, r1) of W (row-major bf16, K columns) times xs (fp32 in LDS); part: LDS, >= nwaves * (r1 - r0) floats;
// epi(row, dot) once per row by one thread. Deterministic: per-wave partials are summed in wave order.
// NB columns: the weight vector is loaded ONCE and dotted with NB staged activation vectors (column b at xs + b * KS),
// giving NB partials per (wave, row). NB = 1 is the batch-1 GEMV and collapses to the original indexing.
// ETX_DSL_GU1: rows [gsplit, r1 - r0) of the pass sit ggap elements further on (moe_up's up rows behind its gate rows),
// so gate and up stream as ONE pass. The caller guarantees no wave's segment range crosses gsplit (one base per wave).
template <int EPL, int U, int NB, class Epi>
static __device__ __forceinline__ void dsl_gemv_rows_nb(const __hip_bfloat16* __restrict__ W, int K, int KS, const float* xs, int r0, int r1, float* part, Epi epi
#ifdef ETX_DSL_SCALAR                                    // all of these are the same in every lane: say so to the compiler
K = etx_uniform(K); r0 = etx_uniform(r0); r1 = etx_uniform(r1);
const int lane = etx_lane(), wv = etx_uniform(etx_wave()), nw = etx_nwaves(), nrt = r1 - r0;
const int lane = etx_lane(), wv = etx_wave(), nw = etx_nwaves(), nrt = r1 - r0;
const int spr = K / SEG, S = nrt * spr;
const int per = (S + nw - 1) / nw, sb = wv * per, se = min(S, sb + per);
for (int i = (int)threadIdx.x; i < nw * nrt * NB; i += blockDim.x) pl[i] = 0.f;
const DSL_G V* ubase = (const DSL_G V*)(W + (size_t)r0 * K
const DSL_G V* base = ubase + lane;
#define DSL_WP(sg) (ubase + (size_t)(sg) * ETX_WAVE_SIZE + lane)   // uniform part first: one scalar base per trip
const DSL_G V* base = (const DSL_G V*)(W + (size_t)r0 * K) + lane;
#ifndef DSL_ABLATE_NORED                                 // ablation: no per-row wave_sum, no partial writes (WRONG output)
for (int b = 0; b < NB; ++b) { const float v = dsl_wave_sum0(acc[b]); if (lane == 0) pl[(wv * nrt + cur) * NB + b] += v; acc[b] = 0.f; }
for (int b = 0; b < NB; ++b) { const float v = etx_wave_sum(acc[b]); if (lane == 0) pl[(wv * nrt + cur) * NB + b] += v; acc[b] = 0.f; }
// (row, segment) advanced by one per consumed vector: segments are consumed in order, so this is sg / spr and
// sg % spr without the division (dsl_gemv_accum's walk, minus its second reduction)
int row = cur, seg = sb - cur * spr;
const int off = seg * SEG + lane * EPL;
for (int b = 0; b < NB; ++b) acc[b] += dsl_dot(w, xl + b * KS + off);
// K % 512 == 0: 16 B loads, 4 in flight per lane; K % 256 == 0: 8 B loads, 8 in flight: 64 KB per workgroup of 16 waves
// (the megakernel's 1024 threads; 16 per lane as examples/llm/gemv.h's 4-wave tiles spilled 359 VGPRs at 128 per lane)
// Half in-flight depth (8 dwords per lane) is the DEFAULT since round 34: 4.832 against 4.884 wall ms/token for
// the full depth (3 interleaved runs each, same box), VGPR/spill/occupancy identical (128/8/4) -- the win is VMEM
// queue pressure and 1 MB less code, not registers. Round 32's Little's-law headroom at full depth was 4.8x, so
// half still covers the latency 2.4x over. Occupancy itself CANNOT move here: the persistent kernel launches one
// 16-wave workgroup per CU, so 4 waves/SIMD is fixed by the grid, not by VGPRs -- forcing VGPR 64 via launch
// bounds left runtime occupancy at 4.000 and cost 2x in spill traffic (9.39 wall, 1678 spills). -DETX_DSL_U4
// gate and up rows as ONE stream pass, taken only where it cannot change a bit: every row lies inside one wave's
// segment range both as two passes of n rows and as one pass of 2n (so each row is one wave's in-order sum either
// way, plus exact zeros from the other waves), and no wave straddles gate and up. Saves the second pass's partial
// zeroing, cross-wave reduction and two of its barriers. Qwen3-30B-A3B: n = 32, K = 2048: 8 then 16 segments per
// wave, 4 per row. Otherwise the two passes below run unchanged.
const int gn = r1 - r0, gspr = d.K / (ETX_WAVE_SIZE * 8), gnw = etx_nwaves();
const int gp1 = (gn * gspr + gnw - 1) / gnw, gp2 = (2 * gn * gspr + gnw - 1) / gnw;
if (d.K % (ETX_WAVE_SIZE * 8) == 0 && 2 * gn <= DSL_RCH && gp1 % gspr == 0 && gp2 % gspr == 0 && (gn * gspr) % gp2 == 0) {
dsl_gemv_rows_nb<8, DSL_UW, 1>(We, d.K, 0, xs, r0, r0 + 2 * gn, part, [&](int r, const float* v) {
const int q = r - r0; g[q < gn ? q : d.rpt + q - gn] = dsl_bfr(v[0]); }, gn, (long long)(d.M - gn) * d.K);
dsl_gemv_chunked(We, d.K, xs, r0, r1, part, [&](int r, float v) { g[r - r0] = dsl_bfr(v); });
#ifndef DSL_ABLATE_ONEPASS                                                      // ablation: gate only, no up pass (WRONG output)
dsl_gemv_chunked(We + (size_t)d.M * d.K, d.K, xs, r0, r1, part, [&](int r, float v) { g[d.rpt + r - r0] = dsl_bfr(v); });

source_lines: 4. **L2-warming prefetch of the task's own weights before its wait is a loss** (+2.5-3.5%, 64 or 128 KB per task): the extra loads compete with the previous phase's streaming tail. Cross-barrier prefetch needs LDS staging or a smaller, later window, not L2 warming.

`buffer_inv sc0` does not invalidate the vector L1 here: a consumer re-reading lines it read before gets its own stale copy (64 B and 8 KB payloads stale in nearly every round, same XCD or uncached memory; 64 KB clean because it overflows L1). ETX's DOMAIN acquire and fleet's XCD-local acquire both used it; outputs stayed exact because tile bodies stream megabytes through L1 between reuses. The DOMAIN acquire is now `buffer_inv sc1` (cost: Qwen3-8B 6.14 vs 6.15 ms, none; DeepSeek-V2-Lite 3.78 vs 4.04 ms, 7%); `-DETX_ACQUIRE_DOMAIN_RELAXED` restores sc0 under the stated eviction condition. Even the cheapest correct whole-GPU barrier (5.5 us) costs 3.4 kernel boundaries.

**Overlap (`bench/overlap/overlap_bench.hip`).** A 64 KB fold read by 8 workgroups takes 1.12 us; by all 304 at once 3.24 us (self-contention: this, not background traffic, is most of fleet's 5 us prologues). A second workgroup per CU streaming HBM at up to 3.34 TB/s leaves the fold at 3.24-3.36 us (x1.00-1.04). Streaming on the other CUs of an XCD instead doubles a small fold group (1.52 -> 3.08 us at 4.31 TB/s). The Infinity Cache is not faster than HBM for any expert-sized stream (10-192 MB), so prefetching weights into it buys nothing.

source_lines: What might be removable now is **empty partial zeroing and cross-wave gathering for a row proved to have one contributing wave**, redundant loop guards for fixed shapes, and a duplicate barrier whose LDS lifetime/visibility proof permits removal. Specialise Qwen's proven GU1 row mapping, leave the wave sum and bf16 rounding identical, write gate/up row results directly to their existing LDS locations, then retain the barrier joining gate and up before SiLU. This may avoid gathering zeros from other waves. Down can straddle wave ownership and must keep its required partial order; it cannot inherit the up proof blindly (`gemv.py:183-184,272-275,768-775`). Do not omit real stores, skip the SiLU, reassociate fp32 sums, or replace payload visibility with a relaxed fence.

source_lines: **Lever rule.** (1) *Bound.* Every lever states B in ms/token on the current reference trace (today `results_tiles/tr_all.bin`, build `all`). For body levers, B = 48 x (critical body - serial floor) of the phases it changes (`etx/tools/floors.py`). For queue levers, B = 48 x (start delay - dispatcher jitter). A bound on an older trace does not count. (2) *Pursue.* B >= 0.050: build it, CPU gates first. 0.030 <= B < 0.050: build only as a passenger in a session already planned. B < 0.030: closed without a build, because an A/B cannot resolve it. (3) *Test.* At least 3 interleaved pairs on one GPU, bit-identical output or 32/32 + CHECK, device median, with wall printed beside it. The verdict follows `examples/vllm_llm/tile_ab.py`: KEEP when every pair is faster and the mean is <= -0.030; NEUTRAL when |mean| < 0.030; SLOWER at >= +0.030; MIXED otherwise. (4) *Act.* KEEP: make it a default in the next commit, then rebase every bound on the new trace. NEUTRAL or SLOWER: close it and record it in the settled list. MIXED: one more session with 5 pairs, then close it unless KEEP. At most two GPU sessions per lever. (5) *The 0.030-0.050 band.* A KEEP in this band is real on the device basis (above the 0.017-0.028 same-binary spread, `examples/vllm_llm/tile_ab.py:25`) but below the 0.050 system threshold (`docs/SPEC-nv-reference-2026-10-08.md:167`). Ship it, but do not quote it against vLLM on its own; only the sum of kept levers, measured in one session against vLLM, is quoted.

source_lines: **Lever rule.** (1) *Bound.* Every lever states B in ms/token on the current reference trace (today `results_tiles/tr_all.bin`, build `all`). For body levers, B = 48 x (critical body - serial floor) of the phases it changes (`etx/tools/floors.py`). For queue levers, B = 48 x (start delay - dispatcher jitter). A bound on an older trace does not count. (2) *Pursue.* B >= 0.050: build it, CPU gates first. 0.030 <= B < 0.050: build only as a passenger in a session already planned. B < 0.030: closed without a build, because an A/B cannot resolve it. (3) *Test.* At least 3 interleaved pairs on one GPU, bit-identical output or 32/32 + CHECK, device median, with wall printed beside it. The verdict follows `examples/vllm_llm/tile_ab.py`: KEEP when every pair is faster and the mean is <= -0.030; NEUTRAL when |mean| < 0.030; SLOWER at >= +0.030; MIXED otherwise. (4) *Act.* KEEP: make it a default in the next commit, then rebase every bound on the new trace. NEUTRAL or SLOWER: close it and record it in the settled list. MIXED: one more session with 5 pairs, then close it unless KEEP. At most two GPU sessions per lever. (5) *The 0.030-0.050 band.* A KEEP in this band is real on the device basis (above the 0.017-0.028 same-binary spread, `examples/vllm_llm/tile_ab.py:25`) but below the 0.050 system threshold (`docs/SPEC-nv-reference-2026-10-08.md:167`). Ship it, but do not quote it against vLLM on its own; only the sum of kept levers, measured in one session against vLLM, is quoted.

VERDICT 3 WEAK
Decided by: `docs/FLOORS-2026-10-08.md:319`, with `docs/PLAN-300TOKS-2026-10-11.md:66`.
Evidence: each of the three buckets is misclassified in part:
- **Removable.** Under the owner protocol, the four non-owner partitions still "acquire that publication" (PLAN:66). The 52.4 us prep->attn edge therefore becomes a mid-body wait on 4 of 5 partitions rather than disappearing.
- **Movable only.** BAR2's +0.095 ms came from a build that also raised the megakernel's LDS from 41,448 to 61,952 B (`docs/RESULTS-2026-10-01.md:98`), and its cause "is not known" (FLOORS:319). It is not evidence that the 231.2 us "reappears, larger" (DEP:160).
- **Irreducible.** The 529.7 us includes the 217.7 us after-take pool that the same ledger registers as an open touch question (DEP:260-261).
source_lines: The argument prefetch `ETX_VL_ARGPF` was measured as neutral, -0.003 ms. `ETX_VL_BAR2` was the build that was 0.095 ms slower. BAR2 raised the LDS of the megakernel from 41,448 B to 61,952 B. Source: `docs/RESULTS-2026-10-01.md:97-98`. Explain these two results before a new prefetch design. The cause of the BAR2 result is not known. Occupancy does not explain it: the workgroup has 1024 threads and 128 VGPRs, so each CU holds 1 workgroup with or without BAR2, and 61,952 B is less than 64 KB. Thus BAR2 is not evidence against LDS staging for prefetch. The ISA comparison is in `/workspace/isa_r11/BAR2_cmp/README.md`. The +0.095 ms belongs to the round 2 pair (tile `79d4b4f`, topk fold on, 59,978 tasks). MATCH with BAR2 was never measured. In that pair, BAR2 has fewer spills (13 to 10) and fewer scratch accesses (21 to 13). The tile-body `ds_*` instructions and offsets are identical, so bank conflicts do not change. The extra 20,504 B of LDS is 20,480 B plus 24 B. The compiler (promote-alloca) put `nx_task` in LDS, 20 B per lane for 1024 lanes. The other 24 B is the second parity slot. In the base build, thread 0 loads the next task descriptor (3 `global_load`) before the event wait, so the wait hides the load. In the BAR2 build, these loads come after the event wait and before the body, followed by `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)`. This adds one round trip before each task body. Hypothesis, not verified: this exposed round trip causes the +0.095 ms. The denominator is the critical-path task count from `trace_r2_base.bin`: 388 tasks, joined by 387 dependency edges and 0 same-worker queue edges. 0.095 ms / 388 is about 0.24 us per critical task. BAR2 also removed 2 barriers, about 0.02 ms each (RESULTS). With these added back, the gross cost is about 0.135 ms / 388, about 0.35 us. Both values are less than one full round trip (0.50 to 0.69 us), so the data supports one extra load per critical task with part of its round trip exposed. No BAR2 trace exists in `results_2026-10-01/round2/` (only `trace_r2_base.bin`), so a new BAR2 traced run is necessary to verify it.

source_lines: Keep the current head-affine parallel partitions. Assign an owner for each `(step, layer, kv_head)`, with exactly one prep execution. The owner performs the existing q/k norm and RoPE, preserves its bf16 rounding and writes the current KV row once. After **all owner waves' stores have drained**, publish a head-local, epoch-qualified `prep_ready`. Publish it **before** the owner executes its attention partition, not at the end of the whole task. The other partitions acquire that publication and run their unchanged imported attention calls in parallel. The owner also runs its own partition.

source_lines: The argument prefetch `ETX_VL_ARGPF` was measured as neutral, -0.003 ms. `ETX_VL_BAR2` was the build that was 0.095 ms slower. BAR2 raised the LDS of the megakernel from 41,448 B to 61,952 B. Source: `docs/RESULTS-2026-10-01.md:97-98`. Explain these two results before a new prefetch design. The cause of the BAR2 result is not known. Occupancy does not explain it: the workgroup has 1024 threads and 128 VGPRs, so each CU holds 1 workgroup with or without BAR2, and 61,952 B is less than 64 KB. Thus BAR2 is not evidence against LDS staging for prefetch. The ISA comparison is in `/workspace/isa_r11/BAR2_cmp/README.md`. The +0.095 ms belongs to the round 2 pair (tile `79d4b4f`, topk fold on, 59,978 tasks). MATCH with BAR2 was never measured. In that pair, BAR2 has fewer spills (13 to 10) and fewer scratch accesses (21 to 13). The tile-body `ds_*` instructions and offsets are identical, so bank conflicts do not change. The extra 20,504 B of LDS is 20,480 B plus 24 B. The compiler (promote-alloca) put `nx_task` in LDS, 20 B per lane for 1024 lanes. The other 24 B is the second parity slot. In the base build, thread 0 loads the next task descriptor (3 `global_load`) before the event wait, so the wait hides the load. In the BAR2 build, these loads come after the event wait and before the body, followed by `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)`. This adds one round trip before each task body. Hypothesis, not verified: this exposed round trip causes the +0.095 ms. The denominator is the critical-path task count from `trace_r2_base.bin`: 388 tasks, joined by 387 dependency edges and 0 same-worker queue edges. 0.095 ms / 388 is about 0.24 us per critical task. BAR2 also removed 2 barriers, about 0.02 ms each (RESULTS). With these added back, the gross cost is about 0.135 ms / 388, about 0.35 us. Both values are less than one full round trip (0.50 to 0.69 us), so the data supports one extra load per critical task with part of its round trip exposed. No BAR2 trace exists in `results_2026-10-01/round2/` (only `trace_r2_base.bin`), so a new BAR2 traced run is necessary to verify it.

source_lines: The per-phase bandwidth shares above divide each phase's achieved GB/s by the whole device's 4.3 TB/s. No phase runs on all eight XCDs. `latency.txt` already measures the per-phase `XCDs live` column (`docs/xcd-timeline-2026-10-11/latency.txt:5-14`). One XCD's share of the achievable 4.3 TB/s is `4.3 / 8 = 0.5375 TB/s` [E], so a phase's own ceiling is `XCDs live x 0.5375 TB/s`, and its share of that ceiling is the only bandwidth number that means anything for it. A phase on four XCDs could never have reached 4.3 TB/s; comparing it to 4.3 TB/s makes latency-bound phases look like they waste bandwidth they never had.

source_lines: One precision about what "idle" means here. `any body` marks an XCD busy when at least one of its 38 workers is in a task body. At worker granularity the busy share is lower: bodies cover 40.03% of worker-time (bytes 27.57% + machinery 12.46%, `account.txt:8-9`), and 53.00% of worker-time is dependency wait (`account.txt:6-7`). A worker in a dependency wait has already taken its next task and still occupies its CU; the 27.06% counts XCDs with no body at all, where all 38 workers are waiting or done. Both numbers matter below: the first says how much work could in principle be re-issued, the second says how much of the machine has nothing issued at all.

Evidence: three of the four supporting reasons are misread, and the bound's arithmetic overstates it:
- **The doubling.** 1.52 -> 3.08 us is at a 4.31 TB/s background (:15-16). At the 0.67-1.71 TB/s the prefetches would add, the same bench gives 3.24 -> 3.32-3.36 us, +2.5-3.7% (:11-13).
- **Level-independent latency.** The cited figure is loaded, with 303 CUs streaming (MODEL:321). The latency phases run lightly loaded, where an idle round trip costs 0.143/0.261/0.412 us from L2/MALL/HBM (`docs/MODEL-vllm-kernels.md:320`).
- **86%.** That is the MALL occupancy *with* a prefetched layer added (PF:32). The KV cache alone fills `103.7/256 = 40.5%` [E].
- **The bound's arithmetic.** `702.3 x 0.172` treats a rate gain as a time saving. The time saving is `1 - 3.61/4.23 = 14.7%`, so the upper end is **102.9 us**; the central value is `1 - 3.43/3.74 = 8.3%`, **58.2 us** [E].

sentence: Within claim 9's own arithmetic, no single figure can flip the verdict. One pool would have to grow by `0.847 - 0.254 = 0.593 ms`. The nearest candidate, the prefetch bound, would have to reach `0.847 - 0.110 - 0.023 = 0.714 ms`. That is 6.9 times its corrected 102.9 us upper end (5.9 times the stated 120.8), and more than the entire 702.3 us of byte time in qkv, o_proj and moe_down [E]. The 0.847 ms need cannot be wrong by that much: the on-arm rounds span 0.011 ms (`R/job2_run4.log:144`).

source_lines: The argument prefetch `ETX_VL_ARGPF` was measured as neutral, -0.003 ms. `ETX_VL_BAR2` was the build that was 0.095 ms slower. BAR2 raised the LDS of the megakernel from 41,448 B to 61,952 B. Source: `docs/RESULTS-2026-10-01.md:97-98`. Explain these two results before a new prefetch design. The cause of the BAR2 result is not known. Occupancy does not explain it: the workgroup has 1024 threads and 128 VGPRs, so each CU holds 1 workgroup with or without BAR2, and 61,952 B is less than 64 KB. Thus BAR2 is not evidence against LDS staging for prefetch. The ISA comparison is in `/workspace/isa_r11/BAR2_cmp/README.md`. The +0.095 ms belongs to the round 2 pair (tile `79d4b4f`, topk fold on, 59,978 tasks). MATCH with BAR2 was never measured. In that pair, BAR2 has fewer spills (13 to 10) and fewer scratch accesses (21 to 13). The tile-body `ds_*` instructions and offsets are identical, so bank conflicts do not change. The extra 20,504 B of LDS is 20,480 B plus 24 B. The compiler (promote-alloca) put `nx_task` in LDS, 20 B per lane for 1024 lanes. The other 24 B is the second parity slot. In the base build, thread 0 loads the next task descriptor (3 `global_load`) before the event wait, so the wait hides the load. In the BAR2 build, these loads come after the event wait and before the body, followed by `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)`. This adds one round trip before each task body. Hypothesis, not verified: this exposed round trip causes the +0.095 ms. The denominator is the critical-path task count from `trace_r2_base.bin`: 388 tasks, joined by 387 dependency edges and 0 same-worker queue edges. 0.095 ms / 388 is about 0.24 us per critical task. BAR2 also removed 2 barriers, about 0.02 ms each (RESULTS). With these added back, the gross cost is about 0.135 ms / 388, about 0.35 us. Both values are less than one full round trip (0.50 to 0.69 us), so the data supports one extra load per critical task with part of its round trip exposed. No BAR2 trace exists in `results_2026-10-01/round2/` (only `trace_r2_base.bin`), so a new BAR2 traced run is necessary to verify it.

source_lines: The per-phase bandwidth shares above divide each phase's achieved GB/s by the whole device's 4.3 TB/s. No phase runs on all eight XCDs. `latency.txt` already measures the per-phase `XCDs live` column (`docs/xcd-timeline-2026-10-11/latency.txt:5-14`). One XCD's share of the achievable 4.3 TB/s is `4.3 / 8 = 0.5375 TB/s` [E], so a phase's own ceiling is `XCDs live x 0.5375 TB/s`, and its share of that ceiling is the only bandwidth number that means anything for it. A phase on four XCDs could never have reached 4.3 TB/s; comparing it to 4.3 TB/s makes latency-bound phases look like they waste bandwidth they never had.

source_lines: **Lever rule.** (1) *Bound.* Every lever states B in ms/token on the current reference trace (today `results_tiles/tr_all.bin`, build `all`). For body levers, B = 48 x (critical body - serial floor) of the phases it changes (`etx/tools/floors.py`). For queue levers, B = 48 x (start delay - dispatcher jitter). A bound on an older trace does not count. (2) *Pursue.* B >= 0.050: build it, CPU gates first. 0.030 <= B < 0.050: build only as a passenger in a session already planned. B < 0.030: closed without a build, because an A/B cannot resolve it. (3) *Test.* At least 3 interleaved pairs on one GPU, bit-identical output or 32/32 + CHECK, device median, with wall printed beside it. The verdict follows `examples/vllm_llm/tile_ab.py`: KEEP when every pair is faster and the mean is <= -0.030; NEUTRAL when |mean| < 0.030; SLOWER at >= +0.030; MIXED otherwise. (4) *Act.* KEEP: make it a default in the next commit, then rebase every bound on the new trace. NEUTRAL or SLOWER: close it and record it in the settled list. MIXED: one more session with 5 pairs, then close it unless KEEP. At most two GPU sessions per lever. (5) *The 0.030-0.050 band.* A KEEP in this band is real on the device basis (above the 0.017-0.028 same-binary spread, `examples/vllm_llm/tile_ab.py:25`) but below the 0.050 system threshold (`docs/SPEC-nv-reference-2026-10-08.md:167`). Ship it, but do not quote it against vLLM on its own; only the sum of kept levers, measured in one session against vLLM, is quoted.
